manifest.name: rolebox
manifest.description: Agent plugin for major harnesses — DeepSeek Harness (DSH), OpenCode, Pi and Codex: define custom AI agent roles with per-role prompts, models, skills, permissions, memory and multi-agent orchestration.

bundle.text:
# rolebox as a dsh profile bundle layer (contract: docs/dsh-plugin-contract.md §5.3).
#
# `name` points at the cordis host half (dist/entries/dsh.js), which
# default-exports the Object plugin `{ name, inject, Config, apply }`. The
# package root (`main` → dist/entries/opencode.js) is the opencode plugin and is NOT a
# cordis plugin, so it must not be referenced here.
#
# The specifier is PACKAGE-RELATIVE because a bundle-patch row resolves against
# the patch file's own directory (<pkg>/dsh/), so `../dist/entries/dsh.js`
# lands on <pkg>/dist/entries/dsh.js wherever the package is installed.
#
# dsh-client-modules only scans loader rows whose specifier is a package root
# (bare name) or path-like (relative / absolute / file:): a package SUBPATH
# such as `rolebox/dsh` fails `exactPackageSpecifier` and is cached as a
# permanent "not a client package" verdict, so the web client never reaches
# the boot graph. The path-like form makes the scan derive the browser module
# id from this package's manifest (`name: "rolebox"`), so package.json must
# keep its `"./client"` export and the client bundle envelope id must be
# `rolebox` (scripts/build-dsh-web-client.ts).
#
# No web config keys are needed (or accepted): the role-switch UI surfaces as
# a dsh.client slot plugin in the web profile, and the `/rolebox` route is
# served by dsh's own host webserver via its optional `webServer` service
# seam. All other Config options stay at their dsh defaults (roleboxDir under
# $DSH_HOME, all namespaces enabled).
- insert:
    - id: rolebox
      name: ../dist/entries/dsh.js
      config: {}

readme.text:
Turn one coding agent into a configured engineering team.
Specialist YAML roles with their own prompts, models, skills and permissions — run as explicit graphs, with memory that survives the session.

One plugin for opencode, pi, dsh and Codex.
The role picker, opened from the composer: Filter roles searches the 18 loaded roles, each row a display name and a one-line description, and the header names the current selection, Base agent.

What it is · See it work · Install · Roles · What you get · Engine · CLI · Docs

---

A general coding agent is one agent with one prompt. rolebox turns it into *your* configured team: specialists defined in YAML, each with its own prompt, model, skills and permissions, working the same task together. What they learn survives the session — decisions, conventions and lessons persist in memory and come back at the next session start.

On DSH, roles can collaborate through [persistent peer teams](docs/team-work.md): invite complementary specialists, exchange events, claim tasks, and continue work across turns. Team execution on other hosts is deferred. Structured workflows use **declared** graphs: `graph_declare` names each node's agent, brief, and permitted outcomes; the host dispatches entry nodes and workers settle them with `graph_submit_outcome`. Graph nodes advance only through accepted outcomes, with bounded loops and inspectable state.

- **Roles** — 18 specialists on the public [oh-my-role registry](https://github.com/EricMoin/oh-my-role), or write your own in one YAML file.
- **Runtime** — the graph v3 outcome protocol: declared nodes and edges, accepted outcomes, bounded repair loops.
- **Memory** — SQLite + FTS5, auto-injected at session start and searchable from the CLI.
- **Tools** — 32 `lsp_*` language-server tools, `hashline_*` edits anchored to content hashes, skills, references, custom functions and hooks.
- **Desktop** — a 12-tool `computer_*` family: `computer_screenshot`, `computer_windows`, `computer_displays`, `computer_focus`, `computer_click`, `computer_move`, `computer_scroll`, `computer_drag`, `computer_type`, `computer_key`, `computer_status`, `computer_permissions`.
- **Browser** — a [23-tool `browse_*` family](docs/browser-use.md) for semantic web-page automation: `browse_status`, `browse_open`, `browse_snapshot`, `browse_read`, `browse_click`, `browse_drag`, `browse_type`, `browse_press`, `browse_select`, `browse_hover`, `browse_scroll`, `browse_wait`, `browse_eval`, `browse_screenshot`, `browse_upload`, `browse_downloads`, `browse_dialog`, `browse_tabs`, `browse_history`, `browse_console`,
Every screenshot in this README was captured from a live dsh session on a demo workspace. Each caption states only what that capture shows.

readme.section: 1 · Every loaded role, on one page
readme.text: Settings → Rolebox: the 18 roles that loaded, each with its slug, description and declared tool policy.

readme.section: 1 · Every loaded role, on one page
readme.text: Each card carries the display name, the slug at the right (`ai-designer`, `apk-reverse-engineer`, `comment-writer` in the capture), a description paragraph, then three label/value rows — **Model**, **Mode**, **Max steps** — and a `Tool policy:` footer. In this capture every visible card reads Model `default`, Mode `primary`, Max steps `not set` and `Tool policy: none declared`; **no card names a source or origin path**. The header carries the `18 roles` badge, the `Refresh`, `Reload roles` and `Open monitor` buttons, and a right-aligned `Loaded 18 roles · <time>` line recording when the load happened.

readme.section: 2 · Work is declared as a graph, not prompted node by node
readme.text: The TypeScript Engineer loads its own skill, reads the protocol reference, and declares the work with graph_declare.

readme.section: 2 · Work is declared as a graph, not prompted node by node
readme.text: The role does not do the work inline. It inspects the repo and records a baseline before editing — the sample project’s test command → 4 pass / 0 fail, `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 — then names one real design point: `Task` has no completion state at all, so `removeCompleted()` needs one. It takes the minimal, backward-compatible reading — an optional `completed?: boolean` on `Task` plus `removeCompleted(): number` returning the removed count — and passes that decision to the worker explicitly.

readme.section: 2 · Work is declared as a graph, not prompted node by node
readme.text: It then declares `graph_declare · taskstore-remove-completed` and yields the turn so the engine can schedule it. The plan names exactly two nodes and one bounded repair round:

readme.section: 2 · Work is declared as a graph, not prompted node by node
readme.text:
- **`change`** (`change-applier`) — implement `removeCompleted(): number` in `src/store.ts`, add the optional `completed?: boolean` field to `Task` in `src/task.ts`, add a focused test in `tests/task.test.ts`, and run the sample project’s test command and `tsc --noEmit`.
- **`review`** (`verification`, independent) — read the actual files and re-run both checks against the same baseline.

readme.section: 2 · Work is declared as a graph, not prompted node by node
readme.text: The turn closes on the declaration being started (`start.kind: started`, phase `executing`, node `change` dispatched). The capture states no execution budget.
Accepted results come back; the parent reconciles them, re-runs the checks itself, and states what was verified and what remains uncertain.

Both nodes ran in their own sessions, and the verifying node is not the node that wrote the code. The closing synthesis reports the test coverage — `tests/task.test.ts:35-61`, importing `TaskStore` at line 4 — as two behavior tests: a mixed store that removes exactly the completed entry and returns `1` while non-completed entries and `get`/`count`/`all` stay consistent, and a no-op path that returns `0` with the store deep-equal to a pre-call snapshot.

A `Checks` table sets each check against its baseline: the sample project’s test command went from `4 pass / 0 fail` to `6 pass / 0 fail, 17 expect() calls, exit 0`, and `tsc --noEmit` stayed at `exit 0` (TypeScript 6.0.3). Both are the project's own scripts; the reviewer additionally ran an independent scratch probe over empty, all-completed and mixed stores plus `add` / `get` / `remove` / `count`, and the parent re-ran the two required commands after the reviewer settled and got the same output.

The `Risk and gaps` list keeps three things open on purpose: the one judgment call still to confirm (whether `completed` should be required, or the return a `Task[]`); the fact that no git repository exists in the workspace, so scope was confirmed from the file inventory plus the pre-change baseline rather than a machine diff; and the fact that the evidence belongs to the recorded sample toolchain and does not establish current runtime compatibility; see [Node runtime](docs/node-runtime.md) for current validation commands.

readme.section: 4 · One brief in, one outcome out
readme.text: One brief in, one outcome out: the worker makes the scoped edits, runs both checks, and settles node change with the done outcome.

readme.section: 4 · One brief in, one outcome out
readme.text: The recording shows a dsh worker completing its assigned brief and using `graph_submit_outcome` to settle its node. Current workers use the host's native command and file tools. Workers inherit the parent’s authorized task tools with native schemas exposed by default. Node tool lists do not restrict them; discovery and code presentation remain optional; see [Worker tools](docs/worker-tools.md). Workers cannot read or steer graph state. Here the worker's whole record is `cat` of its host handoff, the scoped edits, `cat -n` verification of the edited files, the sample project’s test command and `tsc --noEmit`. It notes that this was not a repair round (no revise input was delivered), makes the three scoped edits, reports `6 pass / 0 fail, tsc exit 0`, and closes on `Outcome done accepted (verdict committed, no refusals) — node change is settled`. The banner across the bottom is the one-shot contract: the record does not accept follow-ups.

readme.section: 5 · Watch the engine while it runs
readme.text: The monitor pane: live sessions and their active role, the engine graph with each node's agent and duration, the repair counter and the run's budget expander.

readme.section: 5 · Watch the engine while it runs
readme.text: The Rolebox view is the live engine view; it sits in the dsh conversation as a tab beside Chat and Trajectory, and the capture shows its earlier sidebar placement. In the capture it reports `Sessions 4` with one active role — the session being viewed runs `typescript-engineer`, the other three run `base` — and `Engine graphs 1`: `taskstore-remove-completed`, marked `complete` and `Done`, with an expander for attempts, results, approvals and budget, a progress bar with the run's counters, and `repair 0/2`. Under `Nodes 2`, each node names its agent, worker session and duration: `change` ran `typescript-engineer--change-applier` for 28s, `review` ran `typescript-engineer--verification` for 38s. `Metrics 0` reports `No samples recorded` and says the pane measures anything beyond the core dispatch counters only while `ROLEBOX_METRICS` is set. No loops section appears in this pane.

readme.section: 6 · The same run from a terminal
readme.text: The same run from the terminal: rolebox monitor as System Pulse, Graphs and Tasks panes.

readme.section: 6 · The same run from a terminal
readme.text: `rolebox monitor` renders the project's persisted dispatch state as a dashboard of boxed panes under a header naming the command and the workspace it read. At capture time **System Pulse** reads `IDLE`; **Graphs** lists `taskstore-remove-completed  completed: 2` with `sess 2  tok 0  cost $0.00` beneath it; and **Tasks** reports `no dispatch activity`.

readme.section: 7 · Logs, filtered by channel and by session
readme.text: Plugin startup, role loading and prompt assembly, one record per event, filterable by channel or by session.

readme.section: 7 · Logs, filtered by channel and by session
readme.text: The Logs view, the second conversation tab, polls the workspace's `.rolebox/logs` directory (in the capture `records 125`, `skipped 0`) and renders one line per record: timestamp, level, title, channel and details. The records shown include the `dsh-plugin` startup lines and the computer-use gate verdict, `dsh-agent-registrar` reporting that no `onSpawn` delegate is wired, `role-loader` warnings that a role declares `graph.orchestration: graph_v2` and that the key is recognized but not wired into graph resolution, and a run of `prompt-builder` `Prompt assembled` lines with their character counts. The levels shown are INFO and WARN, and the controls are an `All channels` dropdown, a `This session` filter, `Pause` and `Refresh`. The view and `rolebox logs` read the same log files, so what ran in the UI is debuggable from a shell.

**Loop mode** runs the same task across N rounds, each dispatched to its own fresh session. `|loop:3|` seeds every round with the previous round's summary (`inherit`, the default); `|loop:3,fresh|` starts each round from a clean slate. The parser (`src/loop/params.ts`) also accepts `on`/`true` for inherit and `no-inherit`/`off`/`false` for fresh, and clamps N to a hard cap of 50. Useful for refinement passes, batch fixes and self-correcting workflows.

**Also in the box**, reachable from the same session: persistent memory (`rolebox memory`), skills and references, `LINE#HASH`-anchored `hashline_*` editing, MCP servers, custom hooks, turn-end copilot functions, and rolebox's own [computer-use family](docs/computer-use.md).

---

Rolebox's CLI and development tools require Node.js 26.4+ and npm. For a source checkout, run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and module-scoped tests with `npm test -- tests/<module>/`. See [Node runtime and development](docs/node-runtime.md). The TUI additionally needs Node's `--experimental-ffi` flag; the test command supplies it.

rolebox runs on four harnesses. A `rolebox/` directory in the **current working directory** takes precedence over the global roles directory; registry roles install with `rolebox install <name>` and deploy with `rolebox sync <opencode|pi|dsh|codex>`. Each harness has a minimum version — [Harness versions](docs/compatibility.md#harness-versions) lists them and why.

| Harness | Config directory | Roles directory | Global skills | Env override |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) | `~/.config/opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/rolebox` | `~/.config/opencode/skills` | `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` |
| [pi](https://pi.dev) | `~/.pi/agent` | `~/.pi/agent/rolebox` | `~/.pi/agent/skills` | `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` |
| [dsh](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh) | `~/.dsh` | `~/.dsh/rolebox` | `~/.dsh/skills` | `DSH_HOME` |
| [Codex](docs/codex.md) | `~/.codex` | `~/.codex/rolebox` | `~/.codex/skills` | `CODEX_HOME` |

```bash
cd ~/.config/opencode && npm install rolebox
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/rolebox && cd ~/.config/opencode/rolebox && rolebox init my-agent -y
```

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc
{ "plugin": ["rolebox"] }
```

opencode 1.x loads the package root (`{ id, server }`); opencode v2 resolves the same installed package through its plugin entrypoint `rolebox/server` (`{ id, setup }`, `src/entries/opencode2.ts`) instead, so no second package or extra install step is needed. What v2 registers — and every surface where it degrades — is listed in [compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md#opencode-v2).

```bash
pi install npm:rolebox     # project-local instead: pi install -l npm:rolebox
mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/rolebox && cd ~/.pi/agent/rolebox && rolebox init my-agent -y

readme.section: from a checkout instead: add "extensions": ["/path/to/rolebox/dist/entries/pi.js"] to ~/.pi/agent/settings.json

readme.text:
```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> add rolebox    # installs the bundle into that profile
dsh plugin --profile web add rolebox       # installs the bundle into the web profile
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/rolebox && cd ~/.dsh/rolebox && rolebox init my-agent -y   # $DSH_HOME/rolebox if set
```

Restart the harness. A non-bundle dsh install instead needs one `- insert:` row naming the profile-relative `./node_modules/rolebox/dist/entries/dsh.js` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — see [examples/dsh/cordis.patch.yml](examples/dsh/cordis.patch.yml). Profile patch semantics, the web role-switch dock, and the `/rolebox` REST surface are documented in [docs/dsh-plugin-contract.md](docs/dsh-plugin-contract.md).

```bash
npm install -g rolebox     # or run from a checkout built with `npm run build`
rolebox sync codex
codex plugin add rolebox@rolebox
```

`rolebox sync codex` registers a local plugin marketplace, deploys installed roles,
and generates public native agents under `$CODEX_HOME/agents` (`~/.codex/agents` by
default). Restart Codex, then ask it to delegate using a generated agent such as
`rolebox--reviewer`.
Private children remain scoped graph targets. The MCP runtime exposes 29 base tools,
including native session browsing and declared-graph execution, plus optional desktop
and browser families. Delegated workers require Codex's host-supplied sandbox metadata
and use native Codex tools inside that sandbox. Read completion through `graph_status`;
this stdio integration does not wake an external UI-owned chat. Details and supported
boundaries: [docs/codex.md](docs/codex.md).

Deprecated entry paths The former `dist/index.js`, `dist/pi-extension.js`, and `dist/dsh-plugin.js` artifacts still resolve as generated re-export aliases, but they are deprecated — new checkouts and profile rows should use the canonical `dist/entries/*.js` paths instead.
---

Eighteen roles are published on the [oh-my-role registry](https://github.com/EricMoin/oh-my-role). `rolebox install <name>` fetches one, `rolebox sync <harness>` deploys it, and `rolebox init` scaffolds your own.

| Role | What it does |
|---|---|
| **emperor** | Top-level orchestrator — triages the request, dispatches planner/executor subtrees, synthesises results with closed-loop validation. Never writes code itself. |
| **software-architecture** | Architecture orchestrator — design, review, ADRs, migration plans, and architecture-shaping implementation through specialist subagents. |
| **ai-designer** | Design director — tiered routing, artifact-first output, severity-layered quality gates. |
| **typescript-engineer** | Graph-native TypeScript engineer — type modelling, runtime debugging, API design, module packaging, workspace builds. |
| **react-frontend** | React/Next.js developer — component architecture, hooks, state, Tailwind, data fetching, accessibility, TDD. |
| **dart-flutter** | Dart & Flutter engineering lead — evidence-first research, engineering briefs, risk-based specialist gates. |
| **jetpack-compose** | Jetpack Compose and Android lead — invariant-driven design, encapsulation-preserving tests, AOSP/AndroidX source tracing. |
| **rust-engineer** | Rust lead — complexity-tier routing with safety, async, API, performance and platform gates. |
| **tauri** | Tauri desktop dev

A role is a directory: `role.yaml` (name, model, mode, permissions, subagents, skills), its prompts, and its assets. Start with [create-a-role.md](docs/create-a-role.md) and the [role.yaml reference](docs/role-yaml.md).

---

| | Default single agent | With rolebox |
|---|---|---|
| **Who does the work** | One prompt for every task | Specialists with their own prompt, model, skills and permissions |
| **Remembering** | Sessions start blank | SQLite + FTS5 memory, auto-injected at session start |
| **Switching** | Reconfigure and restart | Switch role in place; the transcript survives |
| **Concurrency** | One agent at a time | Parallel dispatched workers with engine-managed limits |
| **Autonomy** | Free-form chat | Declared graphs with accepted outcomes and bounded repair loops |
| **Code navigation** | Text search | 32 `lsp_*` tools — definition, references, rename, diagnostics, call hierarchy |
| **Editing** | Line numbers that drift | `hashline_*` edits anchored to `LINE#HASH` content hashes |
| **Observability** | Whatever the host logs | Monitor pane, `rolebox monitor` TUI, channel-filtered logs |
| **Desktop** | None | [12-tool computer-use family](docs/computer-use.md): screenshot, windows, displays, focus, click, move, scroll, drag, type, key, status, permissions |
| **Iterating** | Restart to pick up changes | Edit YAML, hot-reload the asset |

For complementary specialties, [role teams on DSH](docs/team-work.md) provide persistent membership, an ordered event stream, exclusive task claims, and automatic peer wakeups. Members use independent agent sessions with their own role configuration; private child roles stay within their owning role. Team execution on OpenCode, Pi, and Codex is deferred.

For structured workflows, `graph_declare` writes a version-3 declaration — each node's agent, brief and the outcomes it may report, plus the edges that route an accepted outcome — and reports persistence separately from the host's initial start decision. The host dispatches the entry nodes; a worker settles its node with `graph_submit_outcome`, which commits the node's state and arms the next node.

`graph_control` applies the trusted lifecycle commands (failure, timeout, cancel, retry, `budget-stop`, and approval requests with their decisions); `graph_status` reads the recorded state back; `graph_audit` inventories the persisted store. Loops live in declared loop groups with a traversal cap, so a repair can repeat but never forever.

Architecture and the full toolset: [graph-outcome-protocol.md](docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md) · operations: [graph-v3-operations.md](docs/graph-v3-operations.md) · internals: [graph-engine-architecture.md](docs/graph-engine-architecture.md).

Full flags and examples: [cli.md](docs/cli.md). Build a suite with [Benchmarks on dsh](docs/benchmarks.md): response/file assertions, trusted local command checks, a `code-fix` template, independent trials, feedback against a saved baseline after role edits, and offline JSON/HTML results with file-change evidence.

---

Registry roles ship placeholder model names, because a role should not be hard-coded to one provider. Map them once in `role_config.yaml` — `~/.config/opencode/role_config.yaml`, `~/.pi/agent/role_config.yaml`, `~/.dsh/role_config.yaml`, or `~/.codex/role_config.yaml` (the harness config directory):

```yaml
model_aliases:
  provider/tier-1-flagship: your-provider/your-strongest-model
  provider/tier-2-reasoning: your-provider/your-reasoning-model
  provider/tier-3-fast: your-provider/your-fast-model

Unrecognized values pass through unchanged with a warning. Full resolution chain, error handling and hot-reload: [model-aliases.md](docs/model-aliases.md).

> **Upgrading from 0.x or 1.x?** rolebox 2.x (`package.json` currently reads `2.3.0`) runs work through the **graph outcome protocol**: `graph_declare` persists a version-3 declaration, and a node advances only through an outcome its worker submits with `graph_submit_outcome`. An existing (legacy) declaration must be rewritten for the version-3 grammar and started as a new run. A persisted legacy state body stays readable but is never advanced, and this protocol has no incremental node or edge construction tool. See [docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md](docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md).
